literal: On this expedition I also wished to bring you along, but Sanya's passes are perilous—without you they cannot be held."
idiomatic: This time I wished to bring you, but Sanya's passes are perilous—without you they cannot be held."

literal: " He therefore ordered him to return.
idiomatic: " He ordered him back.

literal: When Xiaowen died in the traveling palace the death was kept secret on the return; only when they reached Zhen's commandery was the great mourning proclaimed.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen died at the traveling palace the death was concealed until they reached Zhen's commandery, where the great mourning was proclaimed.

literal: On return he was made Grand Master of the Palace, then soon added General Who Pacifies the Distance and Staff Member in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.
idiomatic: On return he was Grand Master of the Palace, then General Who Pacifies the Distance and Staff in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.

literal: He died and was posthumously given his former generalship and made Inspector of Qingzhou with the posthumous title Virtuous.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously his former generalship and Inspector of Qingzhou, posthumous title Virtuous.

literal: His eldest son Zuan, styled Zunyan.
idiomatic: Eldest son Zuan was styled Zunyan.

literal: At thirteen he was enrolled as a student of the Central Secretariat.
idiomatic: At thirteen he entered the Central Secretariat school.

literal: Clever, keen, and eloquent, he was praised by Erudite Li Biao.
idiomatic: Clever and eloquent, he was praised by Erudite Li Biao.

literal: He was twice promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Twice promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.

literal: Whenever Xiaowen debated back and forth with virtuous scholars and Buddhist monks, Zuan took charge of collation and recording and omitted nothing—he won considerable favor.
idiomatic: Whenever Xiaowen debated with scholars and monks, Zuan recorded all and omitted nothing—he won favor.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He rose to Acting Left Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When Shouchun submitted, Minister of Education Wang Su went out to garrison Yangzhou and asked Zuan to accompany him as Chief Clerk of the province.
idiomatic: When Shouchun submitted, Wang Su of the Masters of Writing went to Yangzhou and took Zuan as provincial Chief Clerk.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and concurrent Administrator of Liang Commandery.
idiomatic: He was General Who Pacifies the Distance and concurrent Administrator of Liang.

literal: When Su died, an edict ordered Zuan to act in provincial affairs.
idiomatic: When Su died, Zuan was ordered to act for the province.

literal: Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng replaced Su in the province and again petitioned for Zuan as Chief Clerk.
idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng replaced Su and again petitioned for Zuan as Chief Clerk.

literal: After Cheng marched out, Liang general Jiang Qingzhen seized the moment to attack and occupied the outer wall of the city.
idiomatic: After Cheng marched out, Liang's Jiang Qingzhen attacked and seized the outer city.

literal: Though it was soon recovered, Zuan was dismissed from office for the fault.
idiomatic: Though soon recovered, Zuan was dismissed for the fault.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Zuan's younger brother Yu, styled Zunqing, was also accomplished in learning.
idiomatic: Younger brother Yu, styled Zunqing, was also learned.

literal: On leaving the purple he was Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and was gradually promoted General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of East Yuzhou.
idiomatic: On first appointment he was Court Gentleman and rose to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of East Yu.

literal: He soothed the barbarians of the left and won their hearts fairly well.
idiomatic: He soothed the left-hand tribes and fairly won their hearts.

literal: The barbarian chief Tian Yizong's sons Lusheng and Luxian had first rebelled against their father and fled south, repeatedly raiding and plundering.
idiomatic: Tian Yizong's sons Lusheng and Luxian had rebelled against their father, fled south, and repeatedly raided.

literal: From the time Yu reached the province, Lusheng and the others all sent letters of respect and could not harm the land.
idiomatic: From Yu's arrival, Lusheng and the others sent letters of respect and could not harm the land.

literal: Because barbarian custom did not know ritual and propriety, he established a National University and chose student youths from the commanderies to teach them collectively at the provincial seat.
idiomatic: Finding the tribes ignorant of ritual, he founded a National University and gathered student youths from the commanderies to teach at the seat.

literal: He also set up the Hall of Honored Martiality north of the city wall for military drill.
idiomatic: North of the wall he set up the Hall of Honored Martiality for drill.

literal: The province's borders were cleared and orderly.
idiomatic: The province was cleared and orderly.

literal: On dismissal and return he met Grand General Prince of Jingzhao Ji on a western campaign and was asked to serve as Chief Clerk.
idiomatic: On return he joined Grand General Prince of Jingzhao Ji's western campaign as Chief Clerk.

literal: Soon, in his former office concurrent with the Masters of Writing, he was made Mobile Office for Bin and Xia; for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Yinpan.
idiomatic: Soon, concurrent with the Masters of Writing on the Mobile Office for Bin and Xia, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yinpan for merit.

literal: He died and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Literary.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong, posthumous title Literary.

literal: His son Biao inherited.
idiomatic: Son Biao inherited.

literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was Administrator of Lantian and therefore entered service in the Guanxi region.
idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's end he was Administrator of Lantian and entered Guanxi service.

literal: Biao's younger brother Rong was granted the rank Baron of Chang'an for military merit.
idiomatic: Younger brother Rong was enfeoffed Baron of Chang'an for military merit.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Staff Member in the Secretariat of the Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: He rose to Staff in the Grand Marshal's secretariat.

literal: Rong married the daughter of Minister of Agriculture Li Jin of Zhao commandery and suspected his wife of adultery with Prince of Zhangwu Yuan Jingzhe; he stabbed her to death.
idiomatic: Rong married Li Jin's daughter of the Ministry of Agriculture and suspected adultery with Prince of Zhangwu Yuan Jingzhe; he stabbed her dead.

literal: In fear he also killed himself.
idiomatic: In fear he killed himself.

literal: Younger brother Fei, styled Zunxian, in youth had will and enterprise.
idiomatic: Younger brother Fei, styled Zunxian, had will and enterprise in youth.

literal: At eighteen he was summoned as chief clerk of the province.
idiomatic: At eighteen he was summoned as provincial chief clerk.

literal: It happened to be a year of scarcity; Fei used the household's grain to make porridge and fed the hungry—very many lived because of him.
idiomatic: In a year of scarcity he used household grain for porridge and fed the hungry—very many lived.

literal: On leaving the purple he was Erudite of the National University.
idiomatic: On first appointment he was Erudite of the National University.

literal: He was gradually promoted General of the Right Army and Commissioner for Harmonious Grain Purchase in Jing and Ying.
idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Army and Commissioner for Harmonious Grain Purchase in Jing and Ying.

literal: Inspector of South Yingzhou Tian Yi memorialized that Fei's father Zhen, in his former post in Jingzhou, had won the affections of barbarians and Chinese alike, and begged that Fei be made Separate Commander of the Southern Route with Jingzhou's fierce troops to act as mutual support.
idiomatic: South Ying Inspector Tian Yi memorialized that Fei's father Zhen in Jing had won barbarian and Chinese alike, and begged Fei as Separate Commander of the Southern Route with Jing's fierce troops for mutual support.

literal: An edict approved it.
idiomatic: The edict approved.

literal: Before long he was acting in South Jingzhou affairs.
idiomatic: Soon he was acting in South Jing affairs.

literal: He was transferred to Inspector of East Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of East Xu.

literal: Liang sent its Inspector of Yingzhou Tian Cuchou at the head of troops to invade; Fei on Shiyang Hill defeated and beheaded him, and for merit was enfeoffed Viscount of Du.
idiomatic: Liang's Ying Inspector Tian Cuchou invaded; Fei on Shiyang Hill defeated and beheaded him and was enfeoffed Viscount of Du.

literal: He died as Attendant and Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Manifest.
idiomatic: He died as Attendant and Inspector of Yong, posthumous title Manifest.

literal: His eldest son Hong, styled Daoyan, had considerable ability and was repeatedly promoted Central Secretariat Attendant.
idiomatic: Eldest son Hong, styled Daoyan, had ability and rose to Central Secretariat Attendant.

literal: In the third year of Tianping, for leaking secrets, he was granted death at home.
idiomatic: In Tianping year 3, for leaking secrets, he was granted death at home.

literal: Du Quan, styled Shiheng, was a man of Jingzhao and fifth-generation descendant of Jin's General Who Conquers the South Du Yu.
idiomatic: Du Quan, styled Shiheng, was of Jingzhao, fifth-generation descendant of Jin's General Who Conquers the South Du Yu.

literal: His grandfather Zhou had been Chief Clerk to Fu Jian's Minister of Education.
idiomatic: Grandfather Zhou was Chief Clerk to Fu Jian's Minister of Education.

literal: His father Yi had been Secretary Supervisor under Murong Chui and afterward lodged in Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Father Yi was Secretary Supervisor under Murong Chui and afterward lodged in Zhao commandery.

literal: Quan was broadly learned and had the bearing of an elder; with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and the like he was summoned together as Erudite of the Central Secretariat.
idiomatic: Quan was broadly learned with an elder's bearing; with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others he was summoned as Central Secretariat Erudite.

literal: Earlier, Empress Dowager Mi's father Bao had died in Puyang; Emperor Taiwu wished to have him brought for burial at Ye and said to Minister of Education Cui Hao, "Of all the Du houses under Heaven, which is most eminent?
idiomatic: Earlier Empress Dowager Mi's father Bao lay dead in Puyang; Taiwu wished to bring him for burial at Ye and asked Cui Hao, "Of all the Du houses, which is most eminent?

literal: I am now about to rebury my maternal grandfather and wish to take one elder of the Du clan as Director of the Imperial Clan to oversee the funeral.
idiomatic: I am reburying my maternal grandfather and wish one elder Du as Director of the Imperial Clan to oversee the funeral.

literal: Hao said, "Jingzhao is finest.
idiomatic: Hao said, "Jingzhao is finest.

literal: Central Secretariat Erudite Du Quan—his family is now in Zhao commandery; he is descendant of Du Yu and among all the Du today is foremost."
idiomatic: Erudite Du Quan—his family is in Zhao commandery; he is Du Yu's descendant and foremost among the Du today."

literal: Secretly summoned and seen, Quan's bearing was magnificent and elegant; Emperor Taiwu was moved and pleased and said to Hao, "This is truly the man I want."
idiomatic: Secretly summoned, Quan's bearing was magnificent; Taiwu was pleased and told Hao, "This is truly the man I want."

literal: He was made Director of the Imperial Clan and ordered, with Du Chao's son Daosheng, to escort Bao's coffin and bury him south of Ye.
idiomatic: He was made Director of the Imperial Clan and, with Du Chao's son Daosheng, escorted Bao's coffin for burial south of Ye.

literal: Quan thereafter treated Chao as kin.
idiomatic: Quan thereafter treated Chao as kin.

literal: Chao said to Quan, "We are close in the clan—why lodge in Zhao commandery?"
idiomatic: Chao said, "We are close kin—why lodge in Zhao?"

literal: He therefore drew him in and settled him in the same lineage in Wei commandery.
idiomatic: He drew him in to the same lineage in Wei commandery.

literal: He was twice promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and granted the rank Marquis of Xinfeng.
idiomatic: Twice promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and enfeoffed Marquis of Xinfeng.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Xiangzhou and Marquis of Wei county with the posthumous title Manifest.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of Xiang and Marquis of Wei, posthumous title Manifest.

literal: His son Zhen, styled Jiyuan.
idiomatic: Son Zhen was styled Jiyuan.

literal: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he died as Erudite of the Central Secretariat.
idiomatic: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he died as Central Secretariat Erudite.

literal: Zhen's son Yu, styled Qingqi, held the post of Gentleman of the Ministry of Ceremonials.
idiomatic: Zhen's son Yu, styled Qingqi, was Gentleman of the Ministry of Ceremonials.

literal: He appropriated official timber and tiles to build a private residence; men of pure judgment despised him for it.
idiomatic: He took official timber and tiles for a private house; pure judges despised him.

literal: He died as Administrator of Hedong and was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Justice and Inspector of Yuzhou with the posthumous title Kind.
idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Hedong; posthumously Director of the Ministry of Justice and Inspector of Yu, posthumous title Kind.

literal: Quan's agnatic cousin Jing, styled Xuanming, was learned and versed in the classics and histories.
idiomatic: Cousin Jing, styled Xuanming, was versed in classics and histories.

literal: Provincial and prefectural offices repeatedly summoned him, but he would not accept.
idiomatic: Provinces and prefectures repeatedly summoned him; he would not go.

literal: Jing's son Yu, styled Yanqing, though his offices were not lofty, passed literature from hand to hand.
idiomatic: Jing's son Yu, styled Yanqing, held no lofty office yet literature passed through his hands.

literal: Serving Qi, he reached only Magistrate of Leling.
idiomatic: Under Qi he reached only Magistrate of Leling.

literal: When Qi fell he retired to teach and died at home.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he retired to teach and died at home.

literal: His son Zhengxuan, styled Zhili, in youth inherited the family craft and devoted himself to the classics and histories.
idiomatic: Son Zhengxuan, styled Zhili, inherited the family craft and devoted himself to classics and histories.

literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang he was recommended as Outstanding Talent and ranked high in the policy examination.
idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 15 he was recommended as Outstanding Talent and ranked high in the policy examination.

literal: The ministry clerks, because the policy essay surpassed Left Vice Director Yang Su, said in anger, "If Zhou and Confucius were reborn they still could not be Outstanding Talent—why does the inspector rashly recommend this man?
idiomatic: Clerks, because the essay surpassed Left Vice Director Yang Su, said angrily, "If Zhou and Confucius were reborn they could not be Outstanding Talent—why does the inspector rashly recommend this man?

literal: He should be given the lowest annual rating."
idiomatic: Give him the lowest annual rating."

literal: They dashed the essay to the ground and would not look at it.
idiomatic: They dashed the essay to the ground unread.

literal: At that time within the realm only Zhengxuan alone had answered the Outstanding Talent summons; the rest of the regular tribute candidates were registered and dismissed as usual, but Zhengxuan alone could neither advance nor withdraw.
idiomatic: Within the realm only Zhengxuan had answered the Outstanding Talent summons; regular tribute candidates were registered and dismissed, but Zhengxuan alone could neither advance nor leave.

literal: The ministry clerks, because the selection period was nearly over, again reported to Su.
idiomatic: Because the selection period was nearly over, the clerks again reported to Su.

literal: Su's intent was to test and dismiss Zhengxuan, so he himself set topics requiring drafts after Sima Xiangru's "Shanglin Fu," Wang Bao's "The Sage Lord Obtains Worthy Ministers," Ban Gu's "Yanshan Mountain Inscription," Zhang Zai's "Sword Pass Inscription" and "White Parrot Fu," saying, "I cannot lodge you overnight—you may come before dismissal is final and finish at once."
idiomatic: Su meant to test and dismiss him, set topics requiring drafts of Xiangru's "Shanglin Fu," Wang Bao's "Sage Lord" hymn, Ban Gu's "Yanshan Inscription," Zhang Zai's "Sword Pass" and "White Parrot" pieces, saying, "I cannot lodge you—come before dismissal is final and finish at once."

literal: Zhengxuan finished all at once on time.
idiomatic: Zhengxuan finished all at once on time.

literal: Su read them several times over and said in great astonishment, "Truly a fine Outstanding Talent!"
idiomatic: Su read them through and cried, "Truly a fine Outstanding Talent!"

literal: He ordered the ministry clerks to record and memorialize.
idiomatic: He ordered the clerks to record and memorialize.

literal: It happened that the Ministry of Personnel selection period had passed; they noted his name and sent him back.
idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel selection period had passed; they noted his name and sent him back.

literal: A year later they assembled again; Su said to the clerks, "Outstanding Talent Du Zhengxuan has come."
idiomatic: A year later they assembled again; Su told the clerks, "Outstanding Talent Du Zhengxuan has come."

literal: They again tested him on the "Ballad of the Official's Rare Vessel" and he completed it standing, the text without a single correction.
idiomatic: They again tested the "Ballad of the Official's Rare Vessel"; he completed it standing, without a single correction.

literal: Su sighed greatly in admiration and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to give him preferential ranking.
idiomatic: Su sighed in admiration and ordered preferential ranking.

literal: The clerks proposed him as Recorder to Prince of Changning.
idiomatic: Clerks proposed Recorder to Prince of Changning.

literal: At that time Su's feelings turned against the ministry officials; when he saw the proposal he said, "The young prince does not exhaust this man's talent."
idiomatic: Su had turned against the ministry; seeing the proposal he said, "The young prince does not exhaust this man's talent."

literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was then garrisoning Yangzhou and choosing headquarters staff with care; Zhengxuan was therefore made Staff Member to the Prince of Jin.
idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was garrisoning Yangzhou and choosing staff with care; Zhengxuan was made Staff to the Prince of Jin.

literal: Later when Prince of Yuzhang garrisoned Yangzhou, he again served as Recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang.
idiomatic: Later when Prince of Yuzhang garrisoned Yangzhou, he was Recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Zhengxuan's younger brother Zhengcang, styled Weishan, also loved learning and was skilled at composition.
idiomatic: Younger brother Zhengcang, styled Weishan, also loved learning and composition.

literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaihuang he was recommended as Outstanding Talent.
idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 16 he was recommended as Outstanding Talent.

literal: At that time Su Wei supervised the selection; the test required drafts of Jia Yi's "On the Qin," the "Pledge of Tang" from the Documents, the "Artificer's Maxim," the "Intertwined Trees Fu," the "Table Fu," and the "Bow Inscription"—he finished all on time, again without emendation.
idiomatic: Su Wei supervised selection; the test required Jia Yi's "On the Qin," the Documents' "Pledge of Tang," the "Artificer's Maxim," "Intertwined Trees," "Table," and "Bow" pieces—he finished on time without emendation.

literal: At that time those who ranked first class in the archery-policy examination were to be memorialized together; the clerks found it hard to memorialize separately and demoted him to second class.
idiomatic: First-class archery-policy candidates were memorialized together; clerks found separate memorial hard and demoted him to second class.

literal: Zhengcang appealed the injustice; Wei was angry and changed him to third class, appointing him Mobile Office Staff Member in Chunzhou.
idiomatic: Zhengcang appealed; Wei was angry and changed him to third class, appointing Mobile Office Staff in Chun.

literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Xiayi in Liang commandery.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Magistrate of Xiayi in Liang.

literal: In the Daye era he and Liu Xuan were both recommended by imperial edict for comprehensive mastery of learning.
idiomatic: In the Daye era he and Liu Xuan were both recommended by edict for comprehensive learning.
